name: Andean Gull
rangeDescription: Andean lakes of ecuador to northern argentina and central chile
description: Handsome hooded gull of the Andes; also ranges to coastal areas in nonbreeding season. Found at lakes, wetlands, and bogs; ranging to plowed fields and farmland, and beaches and river mouths on the coast.

name: Zimmer's Tody-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Local in western amazonia (ecuador in pastaza; peru in eastern loreto); more widespread from northeastern bolivia across central and eastern amazonian brazil
description: Very small flycatcher with a long thin bill and yellow eyes. Brownish-olive above and olive-buff below with indistinct dusky streaks.

name: Banggai Jungle Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Peleng, in banggai islands (off eastern sulawesi)
description: A drab flycatcher with brown upperparts, a paler gray underside, and rufous coloration in the tail, rump, and wing. Shows a pale mark between the bill and the eye.

name: Sao Tome Weaver
rangeDescription: Highlands of são tomé (gulf of guinea)
description: A medium-sized weaver with white wingbars, endemic to São Tomé. Sexes look quite different: the male has olive-brown upperparts and a burnt-orange face and upper breast, while the female is more washed-out dull brown above and buff-white below.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Stripe-breasted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Northeastern india to myanmar, southwestern china, thailand, cambodia, and southern laos
description: Medium-sized black-and-white woodpecker with a dirty-yellow breast overlaid with fine black streaking. Male has a brilliant red crown extending from above the eye to the back of the neck.

name: Blue Eared-Pheasant
rangeDescription: Montane forest of north-central china
description: A large gray terrestrial bird with an elegantly frilly tail. Bright red face and upswept white facial plumes (“ears”) are unique in its range.

name: White-headed Pigeon
rangeDescription: Coasts and forested islands of eastern australia
description: A large forest pigeon with a white head and body (juveniles and females more smoky-gray), and blackish wings and tail. Red eye and eye ring, with a pale bill that has a red base.

name: Barau's Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds réunion and rodrigues (mascarenes); pelagic range unknown
description: A pale, mid-sized petrel with white underparts, dark cap, white forehead, and black margins to the white underwing. In flight, also note the distinctive, dark “M” on the gray upperparts.

name: Phoenix Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds french polynesia to kermadec island; ranges southern pacific waters
description: A long-winged petrel, predominantly dark with a gleaming white belly. Throat patch often shows pale speckling, and birds sometimes appear distinctly pale-throated.

name: White-tailed Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Himalayas from northern india to southeastern tibet, southwestern china, and indochina
description: Simply-colored nuthatch with gray upperparts and pale orange underparts. Difficult to distinguish from similarly-colored nuthatches, but averages smaller than Chestnut-bellied Nuthatch, and has a bright white spot on the tail base and a clean tan vent instead of a white-and-orange-striped one.

name: Swierstra's Spurfowl
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western angola (cuanza sul to huila)
description: Rare and unusual francolin that is endemic to Angola. Note the red bill and legs, mostly white face, black breast band, and black-striped white underparts.

name: Snow Mountain Munia
rangeDescription: Western new guinea (snow mountains) and mount capella (papua new guinea)
description: A small bird of alpine grasslands in western New Guinea. Adult has thick, silver bill, black face, brown back, yellow rump, barred sides and black under the tail.

name: White-billed Buffalo-Weaver
rangeDescription: Southern mauritania to guinea, eastward to southern sudan, western ethiopia, and northern eritrea, and southward to southeastern south sudan, northeastern uganda, and northwestern kenya
description: A big, bulky, long-tailed black weaver. The bill is white in males and black in females.

name: White-billed Buffalo-Weaver
rangeDescription: Southern mauritania to guinea, eastward to southern sudan, western ethiopia, and northern eritrea, and southward to southeastern south sudan, northeastern uganda, and northwestern kenya
description: A big, bulky, long-tailed black weaver. The bill is white in males and black in females.

name: Socotra Grosbeak
rangeDescription: Socotra (off eastern somalia)
description: Handsome chunky gray-brown finch with a massive dark bill. Blackish hood, white ear-patches, and golden stripes in the dark wings and tail make this an easily recognizable species.

name: Hyacinth Macaw
rangeDescription: Interior southern brazil, far northwestern paraguay, and adjacent eastern bolivia
description: Unmistakable huge macaw with cobalt blue plumage contrasting with a yellow eyering and bill base. Found at forest borders, in open woodland, and in savanna with palm trees, where mostly seen in pairs but also in small flocks.

name: King-of-Saxony Bird-of-Paradise
rangeDescription: Central cordillera of papua new guinea
description: A medium-sized bird of montane forest canopy. Male has a yellow belly, black upperparts and bib, and orange flight feathers.

name: Prince Henry's Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Semiarid montane scrub of western china (southwestern xinjiang and southeastern tibet)
description: Handsome laughingthrush endemic to the southeastern Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau and its adjacent Himalayan foothills. Gray overall, with a dark rust-colored face, slate-blue-and-orange wing panels, and a bright white “moustache.” An adaptable species, occurring in and around human habitation, as well as naturally-occurring brushy and scrubby areas such as forest edges and gulches.

name: Ash-throated Gnateater
rangeDescription: Eastern ecuador to eastern peru, northern bolivia, and western amazonian brazil
description: Looks like a ball of fluff with legs and a stubby beak; very short-tailed, with a compact body. Males are grayish brown with a gray face and eyebrow; females are orangey tan with a tan eyebrow.

name: Malaysian Eared-Nightjar
rangeDescription: Southern thai-malay peninsula, sumatra, borneo, and adjacent islands
description: Medium-sized nightjar with a long-necked and short-headed profile; namesake “ears'' are often difficult to see. Note dark face, thin off-white collar, and white slashes on the throat (most visible in flight).
